topic: The attention stack — how phone use fragments cognitive infrastructure
body:
**Focus is not a single skill. It is a layered system. And phone use is dismantling it from the bottom up.**

Think of attention as a stack. The bottom layer is sustained presence — the ability to stay with a single input without reaching for something else. Above that is selective filtering — blocking out competing signals while staying on task. Above that is directed output — producing something from the focused state.

Phone use attacks the bottom layer first. Repeated interruptions — even self-initiated ones — train the brain to expect a context switch every few minutes. After enough repetitions, staying with one thing for 20 minutes does not feel normal. It feels like holding your breath.

Once the bottom layer is destabilised, everything above it degrades. You cannot selectively filter because you keep triggering your own context switches. You cannot produce directed output because the input environment is too fragmented.

This is why "just try harder to focus" does not work. You are asking for output from a stack that has structural damage at the foundation.

The rebuild starts at the bottom layer. Deliberate, uninterrupted single-task windows. Start at 20 minutes. Build to 90. Do this before you try to optimise anything else. Foundation first.

Architecture system is in the link in bio.
